Subject: NeoClinic data handling — post-demo recap & retention options

Elena — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Call highlights
- NeoClinic wants inference in the EU region and the ability to minimize persistence of any PII/PHI.
- Primary use: clinical triage assistant (short free-text inputs, patient identifiers occasionally).
- Target latency: sub-200ms p50 for short prompts; throughput moderate.

2) Data handling asks we heard
- 0-retention for raw user messages that contain PHI if possible, or a strict short TTL (hours).
- EU residency for all logs/audit data and any backups.
- Evidence for key controls: SOC 2 scope, logging redaction, encryption-at-rest keys.

3) Our immediate proposal (what we can do today)
- Option A (recommended): Pseudonymization + 24h KV cache, structured logs retained 7 days, EU-only storage.
- Option B (narrow exception): True 0-retention for a subset of message types (PHI-marked) with audit controls and limited features (no long-term analytics).

Attachments: I attached a short options brief (redwood-retention-options-v1.pdf) and we'll share a filled security questionnaire by EOD. 

Next steps
- Camila: share technical tradeoffs and a short options brief (done).
- Ben: provide a quick implementation feasibility note for Option B (expected today).
- Elena: confirm whether NeoClinic legal needs a formal concession memo or an NDA addendum to proceed with an exception request.

Thanks — please let me know if I missed anything obvious.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Thanks Camila — helpful recap. A few clarifications from NeoClinic legal & security: 

- Our regulatory team will be conservative. For anything that could be considered PHI (names, dates of birth, MRNs), we need either 0-retention OR a documented, auditable pipeline that removes identifiers before any persistent storage.
- EU residency is non-negotiable for storage and backups. Is Redwood able to guarantee no cross-region replication for those accounts?
- For analytics we can accept anonymized aggregates, but any raw logs used for troubleshooting must be under a strict retention window (preferred <= 48 hours).

Two operational asks: 
1) Can you map the user flow where a message is marked for 0-retention vs kept for 24h? We need a clear gating point so our app can mark items.
2) If Redwood can do a narrow 0-retention carveout, what operational limitations would apply? E.g., no long-term debugging, no training, and degraded session restore.

Tom — copying you in case MedSys wants to align on technical constraints.

Best,
Elena Novak
Head of Product & Privacy
NeoClinic
elena@neoclinic.io

Subject: Re: NeoClinic data handling — post-demo recap & retention options

Hi Elena — quick technical note after reviewing the ask and discussing with infra: 

Summary answers upfront:
- EU-only storage: yes — we can provision customer tenant data to an EU-only control plane and block cross-region replication for the account. That covers logs, backups, and model serving state.
- 0-retention carveout feasibility: feasible as an exception for a defined message class, but with tradeoffs.

Implementation details and tradeoffs:
- Marking flow: NeoClinic app should add a request header (x-neoclinic-retain: none|24h|7d) on each inference call. Redwood routing will map the header to a retention policy at the request boundary. This provides a clear gating point and audit trail.
- If retain=none (0-retention): we will (1) not write user text to persistent logs, (2) for KV cache we can skip persistent cache write but keep in-memory per-session for up to the configured TTL (max 6 hours), (3) session restore, streaming replay, and long-running analytics will be disabled for those requests.
- If retain=24h: KV cache persisted to an encrypted EU store for 24h; structured logs (non-textual metadata + truncated prompt hashes) kept for up to 7 days by default. Full prompt text is only in persistent storage if retain != none.

Operational controls: 
- We can add an autosampler to capture one-in-N requests for short-term debugging even under retain=none, but only with NeoClinic explicit opt-in per contract.
- Audit evidence: we can produce per-request retention headers plus logs showing retention decisions; SOC 2 evidence will require an addendum to include this exception in scope.

I attached the draft security questionnaire with our answers (NeoClinic_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) and the ops note that maps header values to behaviors.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — good call. Quick confirmation of next steps and where we landed internally: 

1) Technical path agreed (tentative)
- Redwood to provision EU-only tenant and block replication.
- Support header-based retention policy (x-neoclinic-retain).
- Default behavior: retain=24h for most traffic; NeoClinic may set retain=none for PHI-marked requests. Keep in-memory KV up to 6h for none-mode.

2) Contract and compliance 
- We need NeoClinic to sign an exception addendum that specifies the exact message types eligible for retain=none, and to accept the operational limitations Ben listed. That addendum will be attached to the SaaS agreement and routed to our SOC 2 evidence team.
- Legal: Marissa requested a short concession memo template from NeoClinic legal (if you can provide that, we can accelerate).

3) Next week timeline
- Thu 03/04: Redwood to send a formal exception addendum + draft concession memo template.
- Mon 03/08: Tech sync to walk through header implementation and a short POC plan (Ben, Camila, Elena, Tom).

Elena — if you confirm NeoClinic can accept an addendum and the operational limits (no long-term debugging, no training on retain=none data), we will start drafting the paperwork today and push the tenant provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Warmly,
